messages.content:
What the writer told the tutor about their post while revising (facts about their work and their meaning; take them as true):
- About "Tercero, soy vegetariano (I'm not picky but I don't eat me…": Hoping or assuming the family will cook for him.
- About "Tercero, soy vegetariano (I'm not picky but I don't eat me…": Easy about food, only avoids meat.
A learner of Spanish is rewriting part of a post for Email to a language school:
<<<
Estimada Sra. Morales:

Mi nombre es Daniel y yo soy de Manchester, en Inglaterra. Le escribo porque quiero aplicar para el curso de septiembre. Vengo a mejorar mi español: mi novia es de Granada, conocí a su familia el año pasado pero no entendí casi nada, y estoy muy emocionado de aprender para poder hablar con ellos.

¿Es posible que usted me envíe información sobre los precios? También tengo algunas preguntas. Primero, prefiero un piso compartido con otra gente para aprender. ¿Queda el piso cerca de la escuela? Necesito una habitación tranquila para estudiar. Segundo, ¿puedo traer mi bicicleta? Me gusta montar en bici y quiero explorar las montañas. Tercero, soy vegetariano: no soy exigente, solo no como carne; ojalá la familia pueda preparar algo para mí. Mi novia viene conmigo el primer fin de semana.

¿Me puedes decir cuándo empiezan los cursos? Necesito que me responda antes de fin de mes, porque tengo que comprar el vuelo. Estoy seguro de que voy a pasarlo muy bien en su escuela. Mirando adelante a oír de usted.

Saludos,
Daniel Clarke
>>>
The part: "Mirando adelante a oír de usted."
What is wrong with it: This is an English 'looking forward to hearing from you' rendered word for word. A Spanish reader does not recognise the closing phrase and may find it odd at the end of a formal letter.
What they mean (confirmed by them): Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "Quedo a la espera de sus noticias."
Words they already have as hints: espera, noticias, ilusión, pendiente
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in English, one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Name no Spanish word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in English, or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short Spanish sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"As your tutor, I'd say a formal Spanish letter closes with one set sentence, not a translation of the English line. Build it as a short statement that you stay in a state of waiting, followed by the phrase for waiting, then the noun for their reply (use espera and noticias), and end with a full stop.","example":"Esta semana sigo [a la espera de] la reparación del coche."}
